title: Integrate password reset and deactivation with session revocation

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Credential lifecycle tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/staff_access/test_credential_lifecycle.py

verify.summary: Fresh independent T3 functional proof passed reset/deactivation revocation over three sessions per branch, generic 401 behavior, old/new login, Argon2id/timestamps, stable repeat, redaction, owner-only architecture and confirmed disposable cleanup. Mounted current-source pytest (2 passed) and mypy (26 files) also passed, but a bounded exact-image rebuild failed externally on a files.pythonhosted.org ReadTimeout fetching onnx==1.22.0, so both required exact packaged-image gates remain uncovered; this is an evidence/reproducibility blocker, not code FAIL.

Verification recovery attempt 2 re-grounded identical production/test/probe hashes and made the one scheduler-authorized bounded image build attempt. The build again failed externally: files.pythonhosted.org ReadTimeout while fetching the cython==3.2.9 build dependency for insightface, before a current image or either exact required packaged-image gate could run. The already fresh verifier-owned T3 probe remains current and fully green, with no source drift, contradiction, or cleanup residue; lifecycle stays in_progress and the scheduler must halt rather than loop.

Verification recovery attempt 3 confirmed rebuilt face-moment:dev source identity, then passed both required exact packaged-image gates (mypy: 26 source files clean; credential lifecycle pytest: 2 passed). A fresh verifier-owned probe against packaged application source independently passed every FT-001-AC-008 harm-driving result: all reset/deactivation sessions revoked generically, old/inactive login 401, new login 204, changed Argon2id/timestamp projection, stable repeated deactivation, clean redaction, owner-only architecture and confirmed disposable cleanup. Lifecycle remains in_progress; T3 routes to per-task red-verify.

Adversarial supported-concurrency evidence proved a material FT-001-AC-008 break: after reset bulk-revoked existing rows but before it committed, an old-password login read the prior credential and created a session that remained usable after reset completion. The original session was revoked and subsequent old-password login rejected, yet exactly one unrevoked session remained. This is a task-local transaction/concurrency defect with no operator ambiguity; lifecycle stays in_progress for scheduler disposition.

Execution Attempt 2 fresh packaged-image verification passed both exact gates (mypy: 26 source files clean; credential lifecycle pytest: 3 passed) and two independent verifier-owned observations. The full lifecycle probe reconfirmed complete reset/deactivation revocation, generic 401 behavior, new login, Argon2id/timestamps, stable repeat and redaction. The corrected-concurrency probe observed SELECT FOR UPDATE, rejected the concurrent old-password login, revoked the initial session, found zero current sessions before new login and authenticated the new-password session. Cleanup was complete; lifecycle remains in_progress and T3 routes to red-verify reassessment.

Execution Attempt 2 semantic reassessment confirms the prior stale-credential session race is resolved. Login now locks the StaffUser owner row through credential validation, session insertion and commit, serializing both lifecycle-first and login-first orderings with reset/deactivation mutation and bulk revocation. A fresh isolated packaged-image rerun observed SELECT FOR UPDATE, rejected the concurrent old-password login, revoked the initial session, found zero current sessions and authenticated the new-password session. No material finding or operator question remains; lifecycle stays in_progress for scheduler closure.

The autopilot scheduler closed TASK-005 after bounded Execution Attempt 2 earned fresh packaged-image functional PASS and semantic-pass. The prior stale-credential concurrent-session finding was corrected within the retry budget by serializing login with reset/deactivation on the StaffUser owner row.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-008 RED: password reset or deactivation leaves at least one already authenticated disposable session usable; GREEN: each owner-controlled command updates the principal lifecycle and revokes every current session, inactive login and old sessions return generic 401, repeated deactivation is safe, and credential/token markers remain absent from command output and logs; decisive comparison: all pre-command sessions authenticate, all post-command sessions fail generically and the redacted lifecycle projection matches the contract; artifact: isolated integration output, database projection and security scan.
purpose: Complete the accepted staff credential lifecycle so revoked or changed principals cannot retain uploader access through old sessions.
success_outcome: Password reset and deactivation revoke every current browser session, inactive principals cannot authenticate, and repeated deactivation is safe without secret disclosure.
anti_goals: Do not add reactivation, self-service reset, email recovery, session administration UI or automatic credential rotation.
Do not absorb normal browser-session behavior or Photo endpoint authorization.

forbidden_scope: New staff roles or authorization policy
stop_conditions: Reset or deactivation cannot revoke all current sessions in one owner-controlled operation.
The change would require a new credential lifecycle or external identity provider.
Any secret would be echoed, persisted in plaintext or logged.

constraints: The staff_access owner performs principal mutation and session revocation without foreign business writes.
Password reset stores a new Argon2id hash and updates password_changed_at; deactivation sets active false and deactivated_at.
Existing session authentication observes reset/deactivation revocation as generic 401.
invariants: Reset and deactivation revoke all current sessions for the target user.
Repeated deactivation is safe and does not recreate or extend sessions.
No plaintext credential, token or stored hash enters command output or logs.
verification_targets: Proof starts with one task-unique disposable active principal and multiple sessions in isolated PostgreSQL/application state; each rerun cleanup removes only those sessions/principal and discards task-local captured logs, recreates the known fixture, and performs no production lifecycle operation.
Integration proof covers password reset, deactivation, repeated deactivation, session revocation, inactive login rejection and redaction.
